summary: This survey reports institution-level enrollment and instructional activity accumulated from July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, rather than activity in a single term. It covers undergraduate and graduate activity at postsecondary institutions required to report to IPEDS, with aggregate records identified by institution and, where applicable, enrollment level; it does not provide student-level records.

The Completions survey is collected annually for awards conferred from July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, with institutions reporting their postsecondary degree and certificate completions and related program offerings. The unit is the institution, with tables providing either institution-level totals or multiple institution-by-program or institution-by-award-level records. It covers eligible postsecondary institutions reporting degrees and certificates, and the survey includes both completion counts and program offerings derived from those completions.

The Fall Enrollment survey covers participating IPEDS postsecondary institutions and measures enrollment at the institution level, with multiple records where a table has student-level breakdowns. Traditional academic-year institutions report as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with other or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Eligibility and coverage can vary by table, including restrictions to four-year institutions or institutions with undergraduate students.

The Finance survey collects institutional revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for the fiscal year ending between July 1, 2013, and June 30, 2014, during the 2014–15 collection period. Each record represents one postsecondary institution identified by UNITID; the universe is Title IV-eligible institutions active during the reporting period, with reporting required according to institutional control and accounting model. Separate forms apply to public GASB institutions, FASB-reporting private nonprofit and public institutions, and private for-profit institutions.

The 2014 Graduation Rates collection is a winter collection reporting the status of student cohorts as of August 31, 2014. Its unit of observation is the cohort outcome for full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at eligible IPEDS institutions, including four-year, two-year, and less-than-two-year institutions. Outcomes cover completion within specified percentages of normal time and, where applicable, transfer out; cohort years and eligible institution types vary by table, so the results are not rates for all enrolled students.

Human Resources tables describe institution-level employees and new hires, using Fall 2014 payroll status as of November 1, 2014, new hires during July 1–October 31, 2014, and salary reporting for the 2014–15 academic year. Tables generally contain multiple records per institution, with each record representing a staff category, occupational category, or related classification; eligibility varies by table, and some tables are restricted to degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so the 2014 tables using those dimensions do not contain data for all institutions.

These Institutional Characteristics tables were collected during the fall collection cycle for academic year 2014-15 and report institution-level information for the 2014 IPEDS universe. The universe covers active institutions, including Title IV institutions for which IPEDS reporting is mandatory; some institutions may report for multiple campuses through parent/child arrangements. The tables describe institutional characteristics and services rather than student-level outcomes.

This annual Student Financial Aid collection covers aid received from July 1, 2013, through June 30, 2014, reported by eligible IPEDS postsecondary institutions for students enrolled during that academic year. It contains institution-level counts of students receiving specified aid and the associated total or average dollar amounts, with populations and aid categories defined separately in each table. The collection covers undergraduate and, where specified, graduate students; it is not a student-level file.
